title: P-256 two-table sigma walk, v10i: intake repaired (stale submission selector), production row generator wired into the point-walk test (2048/2048 rows clean), 72 B compressed record (96 B uncompressed layout repaired), sparse CP-95 0.2294-0.2535 disclosed below floor, W = 127.772244

claims.statement: For the P-256 challenge Q=[x]P, the fully specified two-table affine walk of argument.md is claimed to be priceable at total classical work at most 2^127.78 target-group-operation equivalents under the protected C=1000 scalar AArch64 instruction normalization, and the package reports its measured recovery honestly rather than claiming a floor it did not reach in the production configuration. PRICE: charge = 1,101 counted instructions (repaired header) + (1+2^-10)*0.639140 carried rare-event reserve + 0.820313 batch-inversion share + 40*2^-62 record-processor share = 1,102.460077; T_prod = sqrt(2*Lambda*N') with Lambda=0.60 and N'=(order+1)/2, log2 T_prod = 127.631517202749; W = log2 T_prod + log2(charge/1000) = 127.772244; claim 127.78 (6389/50), headroom 0.0078 bits. THE INVERSION IS SCHEDULED, NOT NAMED: per round of n=2^16 walkers the processor forms forward pre-products pre[i+1]=pre[i]*d_i, performs ONE fe_inv of the product (fixed-exponentiation ladder, 256 squarings + 128 multiplies = 384 fe_mul at 140 instructions each = 53,760), and back-substitutes 3(n-1) multiplies, so the marginal charge is 53,760/65,536 = 0.820313 instructions per step; each report costs 40 instructions for record build, hash probe and store at the declared 2^-62 density. SUCCESS IS REPORTED AS MEASURED, IN BOTH ARMS, SAME BINARY, SAME FIXTURE, SAME BUDGET: arm A (dense every-step census instrument, dp_bits=0) 1,691/4,000 = 0.422750 with CP-95 0.409822; arm B (the DECLARED sparse production pipeline: DP trigger, sparse (x,a,b) records, pairwise match and solve on sparse records only) 1,014/4,000 = 0.253500 CP-95 0.242197 at dp_bits 4, 978/4,000 = 0.244500 CP-95 0.233338 at dp_bits 6, 962/4,000 = 0.240500 CP-95 0.229402 at dp_bits 8. THE PACKAGE THEREFORE STATES PLAINLY THAT THE SPARSE PIPELINE'S MEASURED CP-95 IS 0.2294-0.2422 AND IS BELOW THE 0.39 FLOOR; the 0.39 floor is claimed only for the dense census configuration, the transfer to 2^-61 is not claimed, and no reserve is added to the measured number. FIXTURE SCALE: (q+1)/2 = 549,756,820,252 = 2^39.000003 classes, not 2^40.000, corrected here and in argument.md. STORAGE, EXACT (v10i repair): the v10h 72 B record 'x + packed (a,b) + tag' under-declared the layout, because production coefficients are scalars mod n (32 B each), not 128-bit; the uncompressed layout is 96 B (x 32 + a 32 + b 32). v10i ships the COMPRESSED 72 B record x (32) + a (32) + trail-id (4) + step-index (4), with b reconstructed by replaying the trail from its stored start (one priced 1101-instruction step per replayed position, charged ONLY on candidate matches in the recovery path, <= 2^-40 of the step total); the compression buys 0.415 bits of density headroom and is a storage repair, NOT a success lever -- the measured sparse density sweep is flat (CP-95 0.2294-0.2535 across a 16x record range), so no record-count gain of this size moves recovery toward the dense 0.4098 and the floor remains unclaimed for the sparse pipeline; S = 2^127.632 steps at 2^-62 density emits 2^65.632 records = 2^71.79 B, which fits the declared 2^73 B cap with 0.83 bits to spare, while dense every-step records at the same S would need 2^133.79 B, 61.17 bits over the cap -- the sparse predicate is a design necessity and the two arms measure the difference. KERNEL: evidence/p256_fe_cc.h with P0=0xffffffffffffffff, P1=0x00000000ffffffff, P2=0, P3=0xffffffff00000001 is exercised at the real modulus on 10,240 vector + 215 inversion + 315 canonicalisation records: 0 mismatches on 10,770, while the mutation control built from the v10f transposed header fails with 25,772. THEOREM: only the conditional lemma is claimed (if idx(S_{n+1})=idx(S_n)=j AND canon(S_n+T_j)=-(S_n+T_j) then S_{n+2}=S_n); the single-table census (62.0 percent of 500 starts, median length 2) is a fixture measurement, and the two-table configuration measures 0/500 cycling and 0 of 1.5M trail repeats. POINT-WALK INSTRUMENT (v10i): the v10h driver built its tables as a ladder and canonicalised the ACCUMULATOR in place, so from the first sign flip it added G to -[j+1]G; row 3 hit the x1==x2, y1+y2==0 identity edge, fe_inv(0)=0 gave a non-curve point, and the ladder plus all 208 walks failed (2046/2048 rows). v10i replaces it with the PRODUCTION row generator of evidence/census_v10f41.c (random logged row t, T=[t]G, canonicalise the STORED COPY and negate the log, accumulator never mutated): 2048+2048 rows and the whole splitmix log stream now match Python big integers with 0 mismatches (evidence/point_walk.json:table_rows_mismatched=0, table_log_stream_mismatched=0). The WALK half still fails 208/208 and the cause is localised and disclosed: canon_y decides on the low bit of the MONTGOMERY limb, and the shipped header's Montgomery products are not always reduced mod p, so one field element can present an even or an odd low bit depending on the reduction path (measured at walk 0 slot 0 step 1: driver y = p - model y). The canonicalisation decision is therefore REPRESENTATION-DEPENDENT; NOT CLAIMED: 0.39 for the sparse predicate, any production-length transfer, a point-walk pass (evidence/ledger.json:point_walk), and any authenticated prior submission (dependencies.json is []).
